advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile warn_if_cache_write_never_read's per-run docstring/semantics with its whole-file call site in summarize (either scope rows per run, or restate the function as a whole-log heuristic).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:479: `rows = _read(path)` then `warn_if_cache_write_never_read(rows, ...)` — reads ALL rows of the file
usage_log.py:1-13 docstring: 'Process-level token-usage sink ... appends one JSON object per LLM call (JSONL)' — the sink is process-scoped, not per-run
structured_run.py docstring: 'Called over a RUN's usage records (e.g. from ... summarize)' and 'True when a RUN's caching calls all WROTE ...' — claims per-run scope the call site does not provide
summarize builds a `per_model` rollup (usage_log.py:492), confirming a single log legitimately contains multiple models
advisory.finding: warn_if_cache_write_never_read's only call site (usage_log.summarize) passes the ENTIRE process-level JSONL, which spans multiple runs/tickets, but the function's docstrings and the call-site comment claim it operates over 'a RUN's usage records'. Across a multi-run file a single cache read in any run clears the flag (false negative), and several runs each doing one legitimate first-write can aggregate into a false positive.
merged_from: warn_if_cache_write_never_read labels the aggregate warning with model=str(rows[0].get('model','?')), i.e. the first row's model, even though the summarized log may mix models across calls/runs — the reported model can be wrong for the offending calls.
scenarios: A weekly CI job whose REBAR_USAGE_LOG accumulates several plan-review runs across tickets; one healthy run masks or manufactures the warning for the aggregate

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the workflow verify-step builder produces a RunRequest whose cache_prefix equals the supplied shared_prefix input (and is None when the input is absent/empty/non-string).
evidence: tests/unit/workflow/test_shared_prefix.py:128-130: `runner = FakeRunner(...)` then `assert res.status == "succeeded"` — no assertion on the built RunRequest's cache_prefix.
ABSENCE: no `cache_prefix` reference in any workflow test (search_files result confined to test_cache_prefix_breakpoint.py).
advisory.finding: No test asserts that the workflow verify-step request builder maps the shared_prefix input onto RunRequest.cache_prefix (runs.py:325-337). test_runner_agent_step_renders_verifier_with_yaml_shaped_inputs supplies shared_prefix but asserts only res.status=='succeeded' — it never inspects the produced RunRequest's cache_prefix, so dropping `cache_prefix=cache_prefix` (reverting the AC for the verifier path) would not fail any test.
scenarios: The `cache_prefix=cache_prefix` assignment (or the shared_prefix→cache_prefix mapping) is removed/broken; the verifier no longer reads the finder's cache write within a run and no test catches it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use a request-capturing runner in test_runner_agent_step_renders_verifier_with_yaml_shaped_inputs (or a dedicated test) and assert runner.reqs[0].cache_prefix == prompts.shared_plan_prefix(FIXTURE_PLAN); add a case with no shared_prefix input asserting cache_prefix is None.
